analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch hunk adds about 9 lines at head lines 1561-1569, describing how LocalTokenizerBridge.decode releases trailing `<0xHH>` byte-fallback token runs and how DetokenizerV2 holds back U+FFFD so its segment restart cannot land inside a character. The supplied units are base_text excerpts at lines 1645-2464 and do not include the changed hunk. I examined those units and the patch excerpt, and they cover the scheduler, deadline, MTP, sampling, reasoning, tool-call and Qwen JSON constraint documentation, none of which is touched by the diff. No threat-model assets, trust boundaries, attestation, encryption, prefix-cache (T-041), authorization or billing behavior is altered by the change. The documentation describes tokenizer decoding correctness, with no new attack surface, key handling, plaintext exposure or routing change. The described change is in provider-swift LocalTokenizerLoader.swift, which was not supplied, so I could not verify the code behavior. Even so, the effect described is output text correctness and does not touch consumer-data confidentiality boundaries. One residual contract question for integration: if the Swift change landed together with this doc, the byte-fallback decoding should not leak partial bytes or alter the response hash (ProviderLoop+SSEParser). I found no evidence of that in the supplied material. I identified no security regression.
